input:
It should be noted that the staffing ramp for the upgrade project has been set at 18%, and this figure is being maintained in response to the lower alternative that was put forward to the steering group. A ramp below 18% effectively prices the recruitment profile at its planned rate for the full build, in the sense that it assumes every post is filled on exactly the week the plan assumes, no post remains vacant while its work is due, and no allowance is made for the overlap that handover between outgoing and incoming staff typically requires. The costs section of this proposal is built on the profile that the ramp produces, and the cost table referred to there takes the ramped profile as its staffing basis. A lower ramp would therefore leave the cost table unchanged in form while, at the same time, removing the staff on which the table is costed.

The case for 18% essentially rests on the shape of the work rather than on its volume. The upgrade project involves running construction and commissioning against a plant that remains in production throughout, and the posts that the ramp adds early are the posts that keep the existing operation covered while the commissioning teams are being formed. Setting the ramp lower would concentrate recruitment into the commissioning window, where the project would be competing for the very same staff it is trying to release. By contrast, the 18% figure spreads that recruitment over the preceding period, albeit at the cost of carrying some posts for longer. The steering group is therefore asked to weigh the two profiles on that basis: the lower alternative is cheaper in total paid time only if recruitment lands exactly on plan, and it carries no margin whatsoever for the slippage that the ramp is there to absorb. FID is taken on the ramped profile, and a decision to set the ramp lower would amount to a decision to re-cut the staffing basis of the cost table, rather than a saving found inside the existing one. On the evidence of the profile, 18% represents the lowest figure that keeps recruitment, handover and cover together within a single coherent plan.
